items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: I always admired. I like that big fat fella that he was... He'd come walking in.

ctx.x: What numbers come to your mind in that? What would you venture to say?

I would say that, I would think just offhand, I can think of one right now. A sweet suit that he made with Paul Whiteman, the big orchestra. Right. That middle, the bridge, when he came to the bridge. And he made that phrase that he wound up on a ninth change. You see, he came down.

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: I met him out at Paul Merez's house when Vic was in town with Paul Whiteman.

ctx.x: And, of course, I can't forget Vic's Beiderback, the time that he taught me in the middle of the and he taught me in a mist. I can't forget that. That was a lesson that was really a great lesson. Of course, I met him out at Paul Merez's house when Vic was in town with Paul Whiteman. And I would say that covering piano teachers would go back to listening to different piano players. You listen and you learn. And I think that's the way most of the old timers did. They listened and they learned. And one thing about…
Kind of like a Wausau just played for fun. They just go around and listen and pick up things. That's right.
